title: Flow Source
description: Canonical source-of-truth for a flow doc. A `<name>.flow.toml` file conforming to this schema drives the rendering of mermaid + step table + failure modes into the sibling `<name>.flow.md`.

schema_version.description: Major version of this schema. Generators MUST refuse to run if their supported version does not match.

entry_point.description: Prose describing what triggers this flow. Rendered verbatim into the doc under the `Entry Point` heading.

steps.description: Ordered list of steps. Array order IS step order (1, 2, 3...). Each step renders as one node in the mermaid diagram and one row in the step table.

id.description: Stable identifier for the step. Used as the mermaid node ID. Convention: short prefix + number (S1, S2, ...).

name.description: Short human label for the step. Appears in the diagram node and the table.

where.description: File path, systemd unit, container, etc. — where the step's logic lives. Surrounded with backticks in the table.

detail.description: One-sentence description of what happens in the step. Rendered as the last column of the step table.

next.description: Optional explicit successor id. If omitted, the next step in array order is implied. Used to draw the mermaid edge; v1 supports linear flows only (no branching).

failure_modes.description: Optional list of failure modes. Each renders as one row in the Failure Modes table.

trigger.description: What goes wrong (often a step+condition, e.g. 'Step 4 - no DHCP lease').

symptom.description: Observable evidence the failure has occurred.

cause.description: Why it happens; the underlying root cause.
